description: Fluorine is a chemical element with symbol F and atomic number 9. It is the lightest halogen and exists at standard conditions as a pale yellow diatomic gas. Fluorine is extremely reactive, reacting with all other elements except for the light noble gases, and is highly toxic in its elemental form.
uses: Industrial production of fluorine gas is primarily used for uranium enrichment. Most commercial applications use fluorine compounds rather than pure fluorine, with about half of mined fluorite used in steelmaking and the rest converted into hydrogen fluoride or cryolite for aluminium refining. Organofluorine compounds are widely used as refrigerants, electrical insulation, PTFE (Teflon), and in pharmaceuticals, while the fluoride ion is used in toothpaste and water fluoridation to inhibit dental cavities.
characteristics: Fluorine atoms have nine electrons with configuration 1s²2s²2p⁵ and the highest electronegativity of any reactive element. The bond energy of difluorine is much lower than that of chlorine or bromine, accounting for its easy dissociation and high reactivity. At room temperature it is a pale yellow gas with a characteristic pungent odor, condenses into a bright yellow liquid at −188 °C, and has two solid forms (α- and β-fluorine) with different crystal structures.
